entries.title: Gentrification in America
entries.snippet: Governing analyzed Census tract data for the nation's 50 largest cities. Portland (58.1% of eligible tracts), Washington D.C. (51.9%), Minneapolis (50.6%), and Seattle (50%) led; nearly 20 percent of lower-income neighborhoods gentrified since 2000, compared to 9 percent in the 1990s; poverty rate percentage-point change -0.7 gentrifying vs +6.7 not gentrifying.

entries.title: Urban Gentrification Metrics: Four Decades of American City Transformation (the exemplar report)
entries.snippet: The operator's exemplar report (vendored as source-report.pdf): New York City leads with a Gini coefficient of 0.5469 versus the national average of 0.40 in 2013, while Atlanta and Miami follow at 0.57 and New Orleans at 0.56; the Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024 (+225% since January 2000); 48 of the 50 largest metros saw worsening mobility with Houston the sole improvement (+1.1%).

entries.title: Cities With the Highest Home Price-to-Income Ratios [2025 Edition]
entries.snippet: Since 2000, median household income grew 92% (from $41,990 to $80,610) while median home prices jumped 177% (from $122,775 to $339,937); Los Angeles, San Jose, Long Beach, San Francisco and San Diego top the price-to-income list with ratios from 9.6 to 12.2; the national price-to-income ratio is 4.6.

entries.title: List of U.S. states and territories by income inequality
entries.snippet: New York is the state with the highest inequality; the economy of New York City (Gini index 0.5469) relies greatly on high-salary earners.

entries.title: Income inequality in the United States
entries.snippet: According to the Census Bureau, income inequality reached then-record levels in 2018, with a Gini of 0.485, then 0.488 in 2020 and 0.494 in 2021, per pre-tax money income.

entries.title: Demographic and economic trends in urban, suburban and rural communities
entries.snippet: The white share of the population fell 8 percentage points since 2000 in the suburbs, 7 points in the urban core; 53% of urban counties are majority nonwhite; today 35% of urban residents and 31% in the suburbs have a bachelor's degree or more education, compared with 19% in rural counties.

entries.title: Gentrification by the numbers
entries.snippet: UGA real estate professor Richard Martin: 'I found a very large, across-the-board increase in the amount of gentrification in the 2000s relative to earlier decades' — gentrification levels were at their lowest in the 1970s and increased every decade until 2010.
